panels.title: Devices
panels.description: NVMe controllers currently being scraped.

panels.title: Hosts
panels.description: Hosts reporting at least one NVMe controller.

panels.title: Not live
panels.description: Controllers the kernel does not report as live. Such a controller refuses admin commands, so every read failure attributed to it follows from this rather than from the exporter. Counted on the boolean rather than on the state label: the labelled series is replaced when the state changes, so for one staleness window a recovered controller would still be counted here.

panels.title: Unhealthy
panels.description: Devices with at least one Critical Warning bit set in the health log. This is the drive's own self-assessment, not a threshold anyone chose.

panels.title: Failing scrape
panels.description: Devices the exporter could not read this scrape. Check nvme_logpage_errors_total{reason} in the Exporter row: 'open' means device-file permissions, 'capability' means CAP_SYS_ADMIN.

panels.title: Over own temp threshold
panels.description: Devices at or above the warning temperature the controller itself reports. Compared against each drive's own threshold, not a fixed number: across this fleet those thresholds span 17 degrees, from 69.9 C on Intel and Dell to 86.9 C on some Samsung models.

panels.title: Worst endurance used
panels.description: Highest consumed write endurance in the selection. The per-drive breakdown is in the table below.

panels.title: Reporting OCP
panels.description: Devices exposing the OCP extended health log (page 0xC0). Only these can report true write amplification and physical media writes; the split is by drive class, not by vendor.

panels.title: Devices by model
panels.description: Model mix in the current selection.

panels.title: Critical warnings — devices needing attention
panels.description: Only devices with a bit set appear here. Empty is the healthy state. Flags: spare_below_threshold, temperature, reliability_degraded, read_only, volatile_backup_failed, persistent_memory_ro.

panels.title: Controllers that answer nothing
panels.description: Devices sysfs still lists but that no longer answer Identify, so nothing knows their model or serial. Usually a controller the kernel has marked dead. Empty is the healthy state. They are missing from every table that shows a model, which is why they get one of their own.

panels.title: Most worn drives
panels.description: Consumed write endurance, worst first. The drive's own estimate: it may exceed 100%, which the specification allows.

panels.title: Least temperature headroom
panels.description: Degrees left before each drive reaches the warning temperature it reports for itself. A negative value means the drive is already over its own threshold. Ranking by headroom rather than by temperature is what makes a mixed fleet comparable: the thresholds differ by 17 degrees across these models.

targets.expr: bottomk($top_n, (nvme_logpage_composite_temperature_warning_threshold_celsius{job=~"$job",instance=~"$instance",device=~"$device"} - on(job, instance, device) nvme_logpage_composite_temperature_celsius{job=~"$job",instance=~"$instance",device=~"$device"}) * on(job, instance, device) group_left(model) nvme_logpage_device_info{job=~"$job",instance=~"$instance",device=~"$device"})

panels.title: Highest write amplification
panels.description: Bytes written to the NAND divided by bytes sent by the host — lifetime average, from the OCP log. Only drives exposing page 0xC0 appear. A high ratio on a drive that has written very little is normal: at low cumulative writes the figure is dominated by the controller's own background activity rather than by the workload.

targets.expr: topk($top_n, (nvme_logpage_media_written_bytes_total{job=~"$job",instance=~"$instance",device=~"$device"} / on(job, instance, device) nvme_logpage_written_bytes_total{job=~"$job",instance=~"$instance",device=~"$device"}) * on(job, instance, device) group_left(model) nvme_logpage_device_info{job=~"$job",instance=~"$instance",device=~"$device"})

panels.title: Fastest wearing drives
panels.description: Endurance consumed per year, averaged over the drive's whole power-on life. Answers 'which drive will need replacing first', which the absolute wear figure does not: a drive at 50% after eight years matters less than one at 10% after six months. A lifetime average rather than a recent rate, because the field is whole percents and does not move at all over a short window. That same quantisation sets the accuracy: the relative error is roughly half a percent divided by the wear figure, so a drive reading 2% carries about a quarter, and one reading 50% about a fiftieth. Drives up for less than a day are left out; for the rest, check Age in the per-device table before trusting a young drive's rate.

panels.title: Devices
panels.description: One row per controller. See the generator for why each query is wrapped in group_left and label_replace: the columns cannot be joined without both.

panels.title: Firmware slots
panels.description: Firmware held in each slot. A revision in slot 1 that differs from the active slot is the drive's previous firmware, kept for rollback — useful when auditing which drives have been updated and which have not.

panels.title: Namespaces
panels.description: Namespace size against the OCP NUSE field, which counts allocated LBAs. The gap between this and the filesystem's own usage is space the filesystem has freed but never handed back to the drive with TRIM — nothing else on the host reports that.

panels.title: Endurance used
panels.description: Consumed write endurance over time. The slope is what matters; the absolute value is the drive's own estimate.

panels.title: Available spare vs threshold
panels.description: Remaining spare capacity against the threshold below which the controller raises its own warning.

panels.title: Host write rate
panels.description: Bytes per second written by the host.

panels.title: Media write rate (OCP)
panels.description: Bytes per second actually written to the NAND. Only drives exposing page 0xC0 appear here; compare against the host write rate beside it to see amplification as it happens rather than as a lifetime average.

panels.title: Warranty budget consumed
panels.description: Host bytes written as a fraction of the drive's own Endurance Estimate, which is the warranty budget and comes from the OCP log, so only drives serving page 0xC0 appear. Unlike the wear field this is computed from two exact counters and does not move in whole percent steps. It answers a different question, and the two disagree on purpose: a Micron 7450 that has spent 20% of its warranty reports 4% wear, because the datasheet figure is deliberately conservative and the NAND outlives it. Not comparable across vendors either — measured here, the same field works out to 1.0 DWPD over five years on a Micron 7450 and 4.1 on a Samsung PM9A3, matching the Micron datasheet but quadrupling the Samsung one.

panels.title: Write amplification (lifetime)
panels.description: Media bytes divided by host bytes since the drive was new.

panels.title: Soonest to exhaust endurance
panels.description: Time until 100% if the drive keeps wearing at its lifetime average. Only drives due within ten years are listed: beyond that the answer is 'never' and the number is an artifact of the field being whole percents, where a drive reading 1% projects to ninety-nine times its own age. Drives with no wear yet, and drives already past 100%, have nothing to project.

panels.title: Composite temperature vs the drive's own thresholds
panels.description: Thresholds come from Identify Controller, per drive. They span 17 degrees across this fleet, so a fixed line drawn at 70 C would be at the normal operating point for some models and far above it for others.

panels.title: Per-sensor temperature
panels.description: Individual sensors, where the controller implements them. Sensors reading zero are not implemented and are not emitted.

panels.title: Time fraction above temperature thresholds
panels.description: Fraction of wall-clock time spent over each threshold. A sustained value near 1 means the drive is permanently hot.

panels.title: Thermal throttling
panels.description: Throttling currently applied, from the OCP log, alongside the time fraction spent in each thermal management level from the health log. Both read zero on every drive checked so far.

panels.title: Critical warning flags
panels.description: Only flags that are actually set are plotted — an unfiltered version draws one lane per device per flag and is unreadable past a handful of hosts. Empty means nothing is set.

panels.title: Media errors (rate)
panels.description: Unrecovered data integrity errors per second. Any sustained non-zero value is serious.

panels.title: Uncorrectable read errors (rate, OCP)
panels.description: From the OCP log: reads the controller could not correct.

panels.title: Retired NAND blocks (OCP)
panels.description: Blocks the controller has taken out of service. A field a controller reports as unimplemented is omitted entirely rather than shown as zero, so a missing series here means 'not reported', not 'none'.

panels.title: Unsafe shutdowns and power cycles (rate)
panels.description: An unsafe shutdown count that tracks the power cycle count means the host is not shutting the drive down cleanly.

panels.title: Error log entries by status
panels.description: Every entry the drive's Error Information log retains, grouped by status. The log holds ELPE+1 entries, 64 to 256 on the hardware surveyed, and the exporter reads all of them. Diagnostic only. Note that this includes admin commands rejected because the drive does not implement them — including probes from other monitoring tools on the same host — so it is not a health signal on its own.

panels.title: Host byte rate
panels.description: Throughput as the controller counts it.

panels.title: Host command rate
panels.description: Commands per second. Divided into the byte rate beside it this gives average request size.

panels.title: Controller busy fraction
panels.description: Fraction of time the controller spent processing commands. Approaching 1 means the drive, not the host, is the bottleneck.

panels.title: Unaligned I/O (rate, OCP)
panels.description: Host operations not aligned to the controller's internal granularity. A high rate is a direct cause of write amplification.

panels.title: Devices failing to scrape
panels.description: A count, not one lane per device: at fleet scale a per-device state timeline is an unreadable smear. Flat zero is healthy; the table beside it names whoever is not.

panels.title: Devices failing right now
panels.description: Empty is the healthy state. Cross-reference the reason in "Errors by reason" below: 'open' means device-file permissions, 'capability' means CAP_SYS_ADMIN.

panels.title: Devices serving each log page
panels.description: One line per page rather than one per device and page, which is 112 lanes on this fleet alone. Pages 0x01, 0x02 and 0x03 are mandatory, so those lines should track the device count; 0xC0 is expected to be lower, since client-class drives and the Intel and Dell units do not serve it.

panels.title: Errors by reason (rate)
panels.description: "No data" here means no device has ever failed, which is the healthy state. 'open' means the device file could not be opened — install the udev rule. 'capability' means it opened but the ioctl was refused — check AmbientCapabilities.

panels.title: Scrape duration
panels.description: Time to poll one device. Single-digit milliseconds is normal; this exporter issues ioctls directly rather than forking a helper per scrape.

panels.title: Exporter build
panels.description: Version of the exporter running on each host — check here first when a metric is missing on some hosts but not others. The build-tag field is dropped: this project uses none, so it always reads "unknown".

title: NVMe logpage exporter
description: NVMe health from log pages read directly over ioctl. The top two rows are aggregates and topk tables, so they stay the same size on a fleet of five hundred hosts as on one; per-device detail is in the collapsed rows below and is meant to be reached by selecting a host.
